title: Continuous Curriculum Sprint Hub for SDKs, Quickstarts, and Docs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Objective: run a recurring lightweight sprint hub that produces 2 modular SDK quickstarts, 1 canonical docs tutorial, and one guided onramp micro-course per cycle. Scope: JavaScript & Python SDKs, 1 sample app template, and docs reference pages. Success metrics: time-to-first-successful-request for new users <= 12 minutes, 30% uplift in quickstart completion rate, and <= 10% first-week drop-off for bootcamp cohorts. Deliverables: curriculum outlines, authored quickstarts, example repos, telemetry hooks in Quickstart flow, and a retention experiment plan.
acceptance_criteria: Two language-specific quickstarts merged and published with runnable example and CI checks
One docs tutorial with verified structured output examples and code snippets
Telemetry events instrumented and visible in DevX dashboard for funnel stages (start, success, error)
Onboarding checklist documented and handoff notes to Support and Solutions Engineering

progress_updates: Week 1: Kickoff completed; curriculum skeleton posted to Confluence; ENG assigned initial template repo; telemetry schema draft linked.
Week 2: Design prototype for interactive quickstart validated in usability test (n=5); found confusion around API keys—added explicit key troubleshooting step.
Week 3: JS quickstart PR opened (GH #378) with basic CI; Docs draft published in staging. Queueing review from Security for telemetry event content.
Current blockers: translation backlog and verifying telemetry names with infra (ENG-2841).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Docs or quickstarts becoming stale after model or API changes. Mitigation: add a weekly smoke-run CI that exercises each quickstart against the latest hosted API and flags failures.
Risk: Low visibility into real user friction. Mitigation: instrument granular funnel events and link to weekly DevX funnel review with Growth.
Risk: Content authoring capacity stretched by concurrent initiatives. Mitigation: reduce scope by shipping English-first and automating code snippet generation from canonical examples.
